Attachments included: redwood-offline-provenance-summary.pdf, operator-accreditation-template.docx

High-level (TL;DR):
- Sealed delivery: we deliver a signed manifest + accompanying signed image bundle. Signatures are backed by a rotating HSM key in our KMS; on your side we provide an RSA-signed operator acceptance token the moment the courier hands off.
- Operator accreditation: 2.5 hour remote workshop + proctored checklist. Operators complete a short hands-on acceptance in our staging lab, submit the signed checklist, and are issued a short-lived operator credential. Template attached.
- Network fence / airwall: we recommend an outbound-only blocklist with a single allowed egress to our provenance verification endpoint (mutual-TLS) and a local NTP source. We provide a firewall rule bundle and a verification script (we can run the script remotely or you can run it locally).

Mutual action plan (proposed):
1) Security Q&A & acceptance templates (this email) — 48 hours
2) Technical deep-dive call (30–45 min) — schedule next week
3) Operator workshop + accreditation (remote) — within 10 business days of contract signature
4) First sealed delivery & acceptance window — scheduled 3 weeks after accreditation

Operational notes: emergency hotfix path requires a signed emergency manifest, 72-hour acceptance window recommended (can be shortened for SLA uplift).

If that looks good, kimberly and priyom will follow with the technical config and runbook.

Jordan / team —

Dropping the technical details we typically require for sealed delivery + airwall verification. Attaching two reference artifacts: transport-fence-network-config.yaml and signing-matrix.csv.

Sealed delivery (detailed):
- Manifest format: JSON Lines manifest with fields: artifact_id, sha256, signer_key_id, timestamp_utc, signer_signature (detached). We include a chain of signer_key_ids; each key id maps to an HSM-backed certificate in our KMS.
- Signing: Primary signing occurs in a dedicated signing HSM. For customer-private installs we provide a signed bundle and also ship a signed transfer token that includes the courier manifest. The transfer token is time‑bound (default 48 hours) and requires operator-supplied OTP at handoff.
- Acceptance criteria: hashes match; courier manifest present; operator checklist signed; operator acceptance token received and verified against our provenance endpoint over mTLS.

Operator accreditation (detailed):
- Workshop content: security overview, courier procedures, on-box verification steps, manifest validation, rollback drill.
- Evidence required: completed operator-handback-checklist.xlsx (attached), proctored snapshot of manifest verification, and an on-device signed acceptance event.
- Credentialing: we issue operator creds scoped to acceptance actions and limited to the deployment site. Keys rotate every 90 days or on revocation.

Network fence (airwall) recommendations:
- Minimal egress: allow outbound TLS only to: provenance-api.redwood.internal:443 (mTLS), and NTP to your internal NTP pool. Block all other outbound flows by default.
- Verification: we provide a validation script that probes outbound connectivity and verifies mTLS handshake and certificate pins. Script returns a signed verification blob to be retained with the operator acceptance record.

Emergency & rollback
- Hotfix flow: signed emergency bundle + signed emergency manifest; operator performs zero-touch activation with an operator-approved two-person signoff. We recommend a 72-hour staged rollout with an initial canary (single rack).

Notes: we can adapt the transfer token TTL and HSM key policy to your procurement/legal needs.

Attachments: transport-fence-network-config.yaml, signing-matrix.csv, operator-handback-checklist.xlsx (also attached by PrIyom)

Happy to hop on a call to walk through the YAML and the pinning details.

—Kimberly

Jordan —

Following up with the operational checklist and a courier acknowledgement template for procurement. Small additions to Kimberly's notes above:

Operational acceptance checklist (high level):
- Courier arrives and presents manifest + transfer token; operator verifies courier id against PO and signs courier-ack-template.txt.
- Operator runs local verification: sha256 check of images, manifest chain verification, and a local integrity check against an allowlist.
- Operator records signed handback and uploads the verification blob to our secure intake endpoint over an ephemeral USB transfer (we provide the intake assistant binary).
- If any mismatch, operator triggers quarantine and opens a ticket with our incident queue (high priority).

Time windows and resources:
- Standard acceptance window: 48 hours from arrival.
- Emergency acceptance (hotfix): we’ll accept signed emergency manifests with same-day acknowledgement if the courier window and operator creds are valid.

Attachments: operator-handback-checklist.xlsx, courier-ack-template.txt

I’ll attach the intake assistant binary pointer in Drive and can run a remote rehearsal with your operators before the first delivery.

Thanks —
Priyom Das
On‑Prem Operations Lead
